topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by introducing the overarching theme of inflammation initiation and resolution and setting expectations for how previously learned immune components connect.

topics.label: Recognition of Infection and Damage via PAMPs and DAMPs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular cues that enable the innate immune system to detect microbial presence and cellular damage while distinguishing self from non-self.

topics.label: Pattern Recognition Receptor Families and Inflammasome Signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the cellular localization, receptor classes, and downstream signaling cascades of pattern recognition receptors and inflammasome complexes that trigger inflammatory gene expression.

topics.label: Cellular Recruitment and Systemic Consequences of Inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how inflammatory activation coordinates leukocyte trafficking into tissues, cell migration to draining lymph nodes, and the systemic risks associated with uncontrolled hyperactivation.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the mechanisms that terminate acute inflammation, the processes involved in repairing damaged tissue, and the pathological or protective outcomes that occur when inflammation fails to resolve.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing by concluding the session and previewing the subject of the next lecture.
